about: Appearance schema v3 (2026-10-22): one question per renderer parameter (src/city/facade.ts Dress, the style's art and palette), so a label renders directly. Every attribute allows cannot_tell. `type` is the building's overall look, worded visually; its `style` map gives the renderer style each answer draws with.

usable.says: yes: the target (between the red lines; its mapped size is given in your task) is clearly visible — most of its street wall and its full height. several_buildings: what lies between the lines is clearly two or more different buildings (different heights, colours or styles) of which none is the target alone. no: hidden by trees, vehicles, scaffolding, or not visible.

says.painted_wood_rowhouse: a narrow 2-3 storey painted wooden row house: one bay window, ornate trim, a gable or false front, stairs up to the door
says.wood_or_stucco_flats: a 2-3 storey house or flats, wood or stucco, square or rounded bays, a simpler cornice, often a garage under
says.stucco_house_with_garage: a 1-3 storey smooth stucco house with a garage at street level, arched or picture windows
says.bay_window_apartment_block: a 3-7 storey apartment block with stacks of bay windows up the front
says.classic_stone_apartment_hotel: a 4-9 storey cream/buff stone, terracotta or stucco apartment block with a flat ornamented front, heavy cornice, often an arched entry
says.brick_apartment_block: a 4-9 storey red, brown or buff brick apartment block, flat front, often fire escapes
says.spanish_stucco_apartments: a 3-6 storey stucco apartment block with arches, iron balconettes, tile accents
says.boxy_modern_apartments: a plain modern apartment box: aluminium windows, garages under, sometimes colour panels or balconies
says.sleek_modern_apartments: a newer apartment block: large glass, panels or timber, box bays, glass balconies
says.shops_with_flats_above: 2-4 storeys of flats (wood or stucco, often bays) over a row of shops
says.one_storey_shop_building: one or two storeys of shops with a plain front and a sign band or raised sign panel
says.brick_warehouse_loft: a brick warehouse, loft or workshop: big industrial windows, plain parapet
says.modern_commercial_box: a plain modern commercial or office box: ribbon or aluminium windows, panels or render
says.classic_office_block: a pre-war office, bank or hotel in stone or terracotta: piers, big windows, a deep cornice
says.glass_tower: a high-rise with a glass curtain wall
says.chinatown_building: a Chinatown building: painted balconies, tiled eaves, red, green and gold

wall_colour.says: the main wall colour of the upper floors, ignoring windows, trim and signs; a shaded white wall is still white

trim_colour.says: the colour of the cornice, window frames and other trim, if it differs from the wall

ground_colour.says: the ground floor's wall colour, if it is painted differently from the floors above

says.wood_siding: horizontal wood boards: thin parallel horizontal lines across the wall, often painted
says.stucco: smooth or textured render with no lines
says.brick: brick, painted or not: a grid of small joints
says.stone: stone or terracotta blocks or ornament
says.panels: large flat panels with visible joints (metal, fibre-cement, concrete)

says.tall_sash: individual tall rectangular windows, taller than wide
says.wide_picture: individual windows wider than tall, large single panes
says.grid: large industrial or office windows divided into many small panes

says.shops_all: the whole street frontage is shopfronts
says.one_shop: one shopfront (or a shop and a door), the rest is wall, entrance or garage
says.garages: garage doors take most of the ground floor
says.entrance_only: just a front door or lobby and ordinary windows
says.blank: blank wall, loading doors or nothing at street level

says.bracketed_cornice: a projecting cornice held on visible brackets
says.plain_cornice: a projecting cornice or moulding band without brackets
says.brick_corbels: brick courses stepping out under the top
says.plain_parapet: the wall simply stops with a thin coping
says.sign_panel: a raised panel at the middle of the top of the front, above the roofline
says.gable: a pointed gable, or a false front hiding one
says.roof_overhang: a flat roof slab overhanging the wall

bays.says: bay windows projecting from the upper floors: none; one vertical stack; two or more stacks

bay_shape.says: the shape of the bay windows, if any

balconies.says: balconettes = shallow railings at windows; projecting = platforms you can stand on

fire_escape.says: metal fire escape stairs/landings on the visible street wall

awnings.says: fabric or metal awnings or canopies over the ground floor

awning_colour.says: the main awning colour, if any

piers.says: vertical piers or pilasters running up the front between the window bays

colour_panels.says: on a modern front: groups of windows set in panels of a different, often bright, colour
